title: The Deformed Image Vortex Ansatz: A Perturbation-Aware Description of Magnetic Vortices in In-Plane Fields
authors: Thomas G. Coppée, Colin Ducarme, Simon de Wergifosse, Flavio Abreu Araujo
abstract: Thiele-based descriptions of magnetic vortex dynamics in thin ferromagnetic nanodots rely on magnetization ansätze that describe the equilibrium texture but cannot represent perturbation-induced deformations. We introduce the Deformed Image Vortex Ansatz (DIVA): a perturbation-aware ansatz in which the response to an external perturbation is built into the magnetization profile itself, rather than appended to the dynamics as a correction. Here, we demonstrate the concept for a uniform, stationary in-plane field applied to a Permalloy nanodot, for which the deformation is analytically tractable. A symmetry-based perturbative expansion identifies the leading deformation as a single $m = 1$ harmonic around the disk, while energy minimization and a dominant-balance analysis yield a closed-form interpolant for the radial profile. Benchmarked against micromagnetic simulations on Permalloy disks of aspect ratio $t/R = 0.1$ and $0.0125$, this realization reduces the disk-averaged angular deviation by a factor of 3 to 6 relative to the two-vortex ansatz, depending on geometry and field, and reduces the total-energy deviation by about a factor of six in the thicker disk.
summary: This paper introduces the Deformed Image Vortex Ansatz (DIVA) to improve the theoretical description of magnetic vortices in nanodots under external fields. By building the field response directly into the magnetization profile, DIVA provides a significantly more accurate model than previous methods. The work validates this improved theory by comparing its predictions against detailed micromagnetic simulations.
main_problem: Existing magnetization ansätze fail to accurately describe how magnetic vortices deform when subjected to external in-plane magnetic fields.
main_result: The proposed Deformed Image Vortex Ansatz (DIVA) significantly reduces the error in describing vortex deformation compared to previous ansätze, showing improvements by factors of 3 to 6 in angular deviation.
method: The authors developed a perturbation-aware ansatz (DIVA) and minimized the total energy functional by solving a resulting differential equation for the radial profile of the deformation.
model_or_system: The study models magnetic vortices in thin ferromagnetic nanodots (Permalloy) subjected to an external in-plane field. The physics is governed by minimizing the total energy functional, which includes exchange, Zeeman, and magnetostatic terms.
key_observables: Disk-averaged angular deviation ($\delta\Phi$), total-energy deviation, and the radial profile function $f(r)$.
important_parameters: Aspect ratio ($t/R$), external field strength ($H$), and material parameters like saturation magnetization ($M_s$).
main_assumptions: The deformation is assumed to be dominated by the $m=1$ harmonic, and the magnetostatic energy is approximated using a local functional form.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically compares the local magnetization directions for the two-vortex ansatz and DIVA under an in-plane field. Other figures show energy decompositions and the dependence of the demagnetizing factor on aspect ratio.
paper_structure: The paper first identifies the limitation of existing ansätze, introduces the DIVA, derives the governing radial equation by energy minimization, and finally benchmarks the solution against micromagnetic simulations to validate the improved accuracy.
why_interesting: While focused on classical magnetism, the methodology of building the perturbation response directly into the ansatz, rather than adding it as a correction, mirrors advanced techniques used in developing effective Hamiltonians or variational wavefunctions in quantum many-body physics.
